name: Hand controls (webcam gestures)
what: Play with bare hands in front of a webcam. One call opens the camera and runs Google's MediaPipe hand tracker in the browser (GPU with CPU fallback), mirrors it like a selfie and smooths it with a One Euro filter. Per hand you get a stable pose out of 20 (open, fist, point, pinch, OK, V, thumbs up and down, rock, gun, claw...), a score for every pose, palm position, pinch, openness, roll and depth, and events: swipes, push and pull, circles, wave, twist, pinch tap and double tap, throw, hold, and two-hand clap, zoom and steering wheel. Gestures can be switched on and off. Synthetic hands drive the same engine without a camera, for tests, bots and mouse or touch fallbacks. Includes pinch-click and open/fist helpers with hysteresis and plain-words camera error messages.
use_when: the player controls the game with their bare hands through a webcam: pointing, pinching, making a fist, swiping, throwing or clapping
from_game: Show of Hands (the 14 hands games), GODHAND

third_party.what: MediaPipe Tasks Vision (npm dependency; wasm copied from node_modules at install)
third_party.author: Google

third_party.what: hand_landmarker.task model (downloaded from Google at install, not redistributed; no separate licence stated by Google)
third_party.author: Google

third_party.what: One Euro filter algorithm (implementation written from the paper)
third_party.author: Casiez, Roussel and Vogel (CHI 2012)

good_for: Webcam games where the hands are the controller: catching, throwing, pointing and pinching at things, steering with two fists, clapping, calm gesture games, hand-shaped puzzles. Works with any renderer.
not_for: Games that must work without any camera and have no fallback plan; full-body or face tracking (see meticulai-blink-input for eyes); precise finger-by-finger input such as typing. Needs https or localhost for the camera.
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-hand-controls, then add @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.1.0 and the assets script to my-game/package.json (HOW-TO-USE.md, 'Drop it into the starter')
